problems.title: Single-component flags do not mask the optimized supervised loss
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, Eq.(3), PDF p.5; Table 3, p.9; rebind/scripts/sdxl/rebind_lora_sdxl.py, lines 1489–1507
claim: In the ordinary no-SNR branch, active/passive selection flags zero the corresponding logging variables but do not affect the weighted loss returned for optimization.
analysis: Use one active and one passive residual \(r_A=1\), \(r_P=3\), with weights \(5\) and \(1\). The returned mean is \((5+9)/2=7\) under active-only, passive-only and combined flags. The derivative with respect to the allegedly disabled passive residual is \(r_P=3\), whereas a genuine active-only loss has derivative zero. Both source groups are loaded; the combined method itself legitimately uses both.
result: The advertised public flag cannot by itself reproduce a single-component ablation. The code revision or external data selection used for Table 3 is not established.
repair: Apply component masks to the optimized loss itself, for example \(A\lambda n_A^{-1}\sum r_{A,i}^2+P n_P^{-1}\sum r_{P,i}^2\), omitting disabled terms and their loader requirements. Log the same included terms.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a later release ablation-path defect, without evidence that it generated the paper’s original component comparisons.

problems.title: Relative role preference is not an absolute alignment threshold
problems.source_location: Section 4, Bias paragraph, PDF p.6; Table 3 and interpretation, p.9; load_triplet_data, lines 859–928
claim: The paper defines \(\beta=U-M\) and interprets \(\beta\le0\) as an unbiased, well-aligned image. The public pruning path tests relative ordering and does not use its absolute-threshold argument.
analysis: The criterion is exactly \(M\ge U\), satisfied by \((M,U)=(0.01,0)\) or \((0,0)\); it gives no positive lower bound on matching score. At combined weight \(1\), Table 3 gives matching/reversed scores \(63.4,75.5\); at weight \(5\), they are \(57.9,65.8\). The reported direction score improves by \(4.1\) percentage points while matching score falls by \(5.5\). Thus reduced reverse preference is supported, but the stated absolute-matching interpretation does not follow from that statistic. The public filter retains zero and low-score ties because only the sign of \(M-U\) is tested.
result: The relative statistic remains useful within its definition. No real image is assigned the synthetic scores, and human or fine-grained evaluation evidence is not rejected.
repair: Describe \(\beta\le0\) as intended-over-reversed score ordering and report both scores. If absolute quality is intended, separately calibrate an explicit condition such as \(M\ge\tau\) together with \(M-U\ge\delta\); no numerical threshold is validated here.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded logical interpretation of a correctly defined difference score and its public predicate, not a demonstrated collapse of the empirical method.

problems.title: A finite intermediate limit is applied inconsistently across two passes
claim: The first pass slices each relation-type list to the requested finite limit, but the construction pass iterates through the unsliced list and indexes the partially populated dictionary.
analysis: With active relations \((a_1,a_2)\), passive relations \((p_1,p_2)\) and limit \(1\), loading creates only the first relation of each type and its reverse. Construction nevertheless reaches \(a_2\) and accesses its absent dictionary entry. The full-selection default loads all those keys and is a passing control; an image-count ablation is a different parameter.
result: The nondefault finite-relation configuration has a direct missing-key path. This does not show that a default experiment crashed or that Table 10’s image-count experiment is invalid.
repair: Compute the selected relation lists once and reuse them during loading and construction. This prevents requests for unselected relation keys, without guaranteeing that all unrelated dataset errors are resolved.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded later-release nondefault configuration error, with no demonstrated central-paper damage.
